trial_court: Additional Principal Judge, Additional Family Court No. II, Dhanbad (Original Suit No. 574 of 2022)
facts_of_case: The parties are married and the husband filed a petition for dissolution of marriage on the ground that the marriage is null and void under Section 12(1)(b) read with Section 5(ii)(b) of the Hindu Marriage Act, which was dismissed by the trial court.

legal_principles.principle: The burden lies on the party seeking to set aside a marriage to prove that the other party was suffering from a mental disease.
legal_principles.held: Further, medical report submitted by the appellant (Ext.1) is a four-page report which specifically deals with the report of the test administered upon the respondent being Bhatia's Short Battery of Performance Tests of Intelligence, Multiphasic Questionnaire (MPQ) & Rorschach Inkblot Method (RIM) but the medical report of the RINPAS (Ext. A) is half-page report without the report/findings of the test administered upon the respondent.

legal_principles.principle: A party's consent to a medical examination does not necessarily imply that they are suffering from a mental disease.
legal_principles.held: Even as per the report of the doctor also, the respondent was found to be abnormal lady in thought and perception.

outcome.final_order: The suit filed by the husband for decree of dissolution of marriage has been dismissed.

use_for_drafting: preparing a response to a divorce petition
